selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
selected_evidence.summary: Installed and verified the exact two-entry allowlist. Before and after restart, an unlisted user was denied while root reached the normal authorized state.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID a59a9d9a-a5e0-44f7-9ca1-7f28483971e0, received restart acknowledgement, observed new boot ID a6be5e30-c5f6-490c-a7be-212a6e5c1156, and confirmed cron plus the access policy recovered.

commands.command: id; uname -a; if [ -f /etc/cron.allow ]; then ls -l /etc/cron.allow; sed -n '1,40p' /etc/cron.allow; else echo CRON_ALLOW_ABSENT; fi; if [ -f /etc/cron.deny ]; then ls -l /etc/cron.deny; sed -n '1,40p' /etc/cron.deny; else echo CRON_DENY_ABSENT; fi; getent passwd root opsadmin || true; service cron status 2>&1 || true; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
